paragraphs: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda, the Levite and gatekeeper in the Temple. Yuchasin, in the sequence of generations, writes: although the end of HaChalil says that those who shut the gates received their pay in showbread, which is permitted only to priests, this is no difficulty, because priests too were gatekeepers in three places, as related in Tamid. In Tosefta, Shekalim, chapter 2: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda was over locking the gates; Ben Totefet over the keys; Ben Difai over the lulav; Ben Arza over the platform; Binyamin over the ovens; Shmuel over the griddle cakes; Ben Maklit over the salt; Ben Pelach over the wood. Throughout his life he ate ordinary food according to the purity standard of sacred food; see the Mishnah, Chagigah 18b, ‘Yochanan,’ and Mishnah, Yevamot, beginning of Cheresh. He was learned in calculation and astronomy: Horayot 10a. He was Rabbi Elazar Chisma’s colleague; see his entry. He was in the Temple with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah; see his entry. Rabban Gamliel appointed him in the academy so that he would have food; see above, Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri. Elazar Safra testified with him about an animal stripped of its hide: Chullin 55b. At the end of Eduyot, chapter 7, Rabbi Nechunyah ben Gudgeda; but Gittin 5:5 and Yevamot 14:2, concerning that very testimony, read Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda. Therefore Maimonides did not include him (Yuchasin under Rabbi Nechunyah). His brother was Rabbi Yehudah; see his entry. Menachem ben Sagnai lived in his time. His daughter’s sons, or his sister’s sons, were mute but could hear; they were in Rabbi’s academy. Rabbi prayed for them, and they spoke. They knew halakhah, Sifra, Sifrei, and the entire Talmud: Chagigah 3a. In the Jerusalem Talmud, Terumot 1:1, there is an incident concerning Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda’s sons, who were all deaf; all the pure foods in Jerusalem were prepared under their supervision. Gilgulei Neshamot (ג״נ), letter aleph, says: these two mute brothers were the two brothers Eldad and Medad, born to Eltzafan ben Parnakh from Yokheved, Levi’s daughter, after Amram released her with a bill of divorce. Their birth was then in tears, because the divorce had not been wholehearted; therefore they were born mute. They were also mute for another reason: they expressed their prophecy without permission, for it does not say ‘saying’; it is not proper to tell others unless ‘saying’ is stated. Therefore they were afflicted in their speech; see there.
